title: Kotiin annettavat turvalaitteet, hälytysten vastaanottopalvelu ja hälytysten vastaanottojärjestelmä
description: Kotiin annettavat turvalaitteet, hälytysten vastaanottopalvelu ja hälytysten vastaanottojärjestelmä Lapin hyvinvointialue pyytää tarjouksia kokonaisuudesta, johon sisältyvät: 1. kotiin annettavat turvalaitteet Lapin hyvinvointialueen asiakkaille 2. hälytysten vastaanottopalvelu 3. hälytysten vastaanottojärjestelmä edellä mainitun palvelun tuottamiseen hyvinvointialueen omana toimintana. Hankinnassa turvalaitteilla tarkoitetaan erilaisia kotiin annettavia turvalaitteita, joilla voidaan parantaa kotona asuvan asiakkaan turvallisuutta. Hankittavia turvalaitteita ovat turvapuhelimet ja niiden lisälaitteet, paikantava turvaranneke sekä ratkaisu yhteisöllisen asumisen ovivalvontaan. Hälytysten vastaanottopalvelulla tarkoitetaan palvelua, jossa otetaan vastaan turvalaitteiden kautta tulevat hälytykset, tehdään alustavan arvion avuntarpeesta ja välitetään pyyntö edelleen turva-auttajille. Palvelun tulee toiminnassa vuorokauden ympäri vuoden jokaisena päivä. Hälytysten vastaanottojärjestelmällä tarkoitetaan järjestelmää, jolla tilaaja voi ottaa eri turvalaitteiden hälytykset vastaan ja edelleenvälittää ne tehtävänä turva-auttajille. Lapin hyvinvointialueella on tarkoitus ottaa hälytysten vastaanottopalvelu omaksi toiminnaksi alustavan aikataulun mukaan keväällä 2028. Hyvinvointialue hankkii hälytysten vastaanottopalvelua siihen asti, kunnes vastaanottojärjestelmä on otettu käyttöön, minkä jälkeen vastaanottopalvelun hankinta päättyy. Hankinnan kohde on kuvattu tarkemmin tarjouspyynnössä ja sen liitteissä, erityisesti liitteessä 1 "Hankinnan kohteen kuvaus". Kilpailutuksessa valitaan yksi toimitta puitesopimustoimittajaksi. Puitejärjestelyn kautta hyvinvointialue hankkii valitulta toimittajalta turvalaitteita ja palveluita sopimuskauden aikana tarpeen mukaan. Hyvinvointialueen tarpeet voivat vaihdella sopimuskauden aikana, eikä tarjouspyynnöllä sitouduta tiettyihin hankintamääriin. Puitesopimuksen sopimuskausi on määräaikaisena kaksi vuotta, jonka jälkeen sopimus jatkuu toistaiseksi voimassa olevana. Hankintayksikön tarkoitus on tehdä sopimus valitun toimittajan kanssa heti, kun tarjousaika on päättynyt, tarjoukset on vertailtu, hankintapäätös on tehty ja muutoksenhakuaika on päättynyt. Hankintayksikön arvion mukaan ajankohta on lokakuun 2026 aikana. Laitevaihtojen toteutuksen ja muiden käyttöönottoon liittyvien toimien aikataulut sovitaan yhdessä valitun toimittajan kanssa molempien osapuolten tarpeet huomioivalla tavalla. Lisäksi valitulta toimittajalta hankitaan hälytysten vastaanottojärjestelmä kokonaisuutena, johon sisältyy järjestelmän toimittaminen ja sen jatkuva palvelu. Järjestelmän jatkuvan palvelun sopimus on voimassa toistaiseksi. Hankintaa ei ole jaettu osiin, koska kyseessä on yhtenäinen tavaroiden ja palveluiden muodostama kokonaisuus, jonka kaikkien osasten yhteensopivuus on voitava varmistaa. Lapin hyvinvointialueen asiakkaiden turvallisuuden kannalta on tärkeää, että yksi toimittaja vastaa koko kokonaisuuden toimivuudesta. Hankintailmoitus on julkaistu toisen kerran uudelleen, koska kaksi aiempaa hankintamenettelyä on täytynyt keskeyttää hankinta-asiakirjojen muutostarpeiden vuoksi.,

title: France – Maintenance of information technology software – TIERCE MAINTENANCE APPLICATIVE (TMA) d’un système du CEA dédié à la Gestion Intégrée du Patrimoine des Sites (GIPS)

title: Government-Owned Contractor Operated (GOCO) Aircraft/Ground Fuel Services and Fuel Storage and Distribution at Cannon AFB, NM, Holloman AFB, NM, Davis Monthan AFB, AZ and Luke AFB, AZ
description: Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Energy is issuing a Request for Proposal (RFP) for Alongside Aircraft Refueling Services to include managing, maintaining, and operating Government Owned, Contractor-Operated (GOCO) facilities and equipment at Cannon, AFB, NM, Holloman AFB, NM, Davis Monthan AFB, AZ, and Luke AFB, AZ. The Contractor will ensure safe, accurate, and timely handling, quality control, and accountability of all Defense Wide Working Capital Fund (DWWCF)-owned petroleum products under their control. The Contractor will perform required maintenance to ensure facilities, associated systems, vehicles, and equipment remain operational to meet the base mission. The Contractor will comply with environmental protection, safety, and security directives. The Contractor will conduct required training to ensure personnel are fully qualified to perform Performance Work Statement (PWS) tasks. The Contractor shall conduct all necessary fuels operations to support base operations, airshows and special events, deployments, exercises, and contingencies under normal conditions, as well as, during periods of heightened security, inclement weather, or other unique situations. Operations must be safely and efficiently conducted to receive, store, transfer, issue, and account for products with appropriate controls to ensure fuel quality, maintain inventory accuracy, and ensure no environmental impact. The Contractor shall operate and maintain the self-service automated service station facilities, equipment, and systems and ensure sufficient product is available to provide 24 hours a day, seven days a week support of ground fuels. The Contractor shall perform required tasks to ensure fuel is properly accounted for and issued to only authorized users. This procurement will be 100% set aside for Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Business (SDVOSB) under NAICS code 493190 (Other Warehouse and Storage). The Government anticipates issuing one solicitation and awarding four (4) firm fixed-price contracts for Cannon AFB, NM, Holloman AFB, NM, Davis Monthan AFB, AZ, and Luke AFB, AZ. These requirements will be for a four-year base period (December 01, 2026 � November 30, 2030), a five-year option period (December 01, 2030 � November 30, 2035), and a option to extend the contract s for up to six individual months (December 01, 2035 � May 31, 2036).This procurement will be solicited under full and open competition after exclusion of sources. The solicitation will be published electronically on the SAM website at https://sam.gov/. Interested companies responding to the solicitation will be required to register in the System for Award Management (SAM) and Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE). Dates of the Pre-Preproposal conference, in conjunction with the site visits, will be listed in the solicitation or via amendment. Offerors will be required to submit in writing to the Contract Specialist (via e-mail) the name(s) of the individual(s) who plan to attend.

title: Languages Testing for Interpreters
description: Services Requirement This requirement is for: Immigration and Refugee Board of Canada Title: 20260726-IRB – Language Testing for Interpreters Description of the Requirement: Immigration and Refugee Board of Canada has a requirement for service of testing components and test assessments for the recruitment of their interpreter contractors to Immigration and Refugee Board of Canada (IRB). Interpreter Services Contractors (ISCs) accredited by the IRB must successfully complete three (3) language tests with a minimum score of 70% to qualify for a contract: • Official Languages Test: Assesses the applicant’s ability to communicate in English or French. This is the first test administered, consisting of a short 15-minute written assessment designed to evaluate comprehension in one of the official languages. • Hearing Simulation (Oral) Test: Evaluates the applicant’s ability to perform consecutive interpretation between an official language and a target language, and vice versa. These tests are currently available in sixty (60) languages. However, there are only two versions of each language test, and the quality and consistency of the tests vary. • Sight Translation Test: Measures the applicant’s ability to translate short documents similar to those that may be presented in a hearing room from the language of interpretation to English or French. This is the final test administered. Level of Security Requirement: Resource(s) Minimum Security Level Required is Reliability Status. Associated Documents: Request for Proposal (RFP) 20260726-IRB. Proposed period of contract: The proposed period of contract shall be from September 30, 2026, to March 31, 2027. The resulting contract will include three (3) one-year optional periods. Estimated Level of Effort: The overall annual cumulative estimated level of effort of the contract(s) will be for 300 tests. Multiple contracts: Considering that contract(s) will be issue based on offerors qualified language(s), this solicitation could results on multiples contracts. Contracting Authority: Steve Dessureault Phone Number: 514-249-2780 Email address: steve.dessureault@irb-cisr.gc.ca Note: Please address all inquiry questions to the Contracting Authority by email only.

title: IRB Digital Case Management TBIPS
description: The Immigration and Refugee Board of Canada (IRB) requires professional services support to the Chief Innovation and Technology Office (CITO) to advance the modernization of the IRB’s current case management application ecosystem through the Digital Case Modernization (DCM) initiative. This support will enable the IRB to define, design, validate, and implement modern digital solutions that improve the sustainability, interoperability, security, and scalability of its case management capabilities. The DCM initiative is intended to address current limitations in the IRB case management environment. Through this requirement, the IRB seeks specialized expertise to support analysis, architecture, technical design, software development, integration, testing, documentation, and knowledge transfer activities required to modernize the platform in a controlled and phased manner. More specifically, the objective is to support the transition of the IRB case management ecosystem toward a modernized, cloud-aligned microservices architecture and operating model that can better support future service improvements, business agility, data sharing, reporting, and the introduction of emerging capabilities such as advanced automation and Artificial Intelligence.

title: Technical Assessment and Cost-Benefit Analysis on Fuel Storage Tank Systems Life Cycle (Installation, Maintenance and Removal)
description: Amended the UNSPSC of the Tender Notice. Offers. Canada is seeking offers from Offerors to provide a Technical Assessment and Cost-Benefit Analysis on Fuel Storage Tank Systems Life Cycle (Installation, Maintenance and Removal) to Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) as described in Annex Statement of Work. The technical assessment and cost-benefit analysis will evaluate various options for the installation, maintenance, and decommissioning of storage tank systems and how they align with current industry practices in Canada. The analysis must identify associated environmental impacts, resource requirements, benefits, challenges, and operational and policy risks such as regulatory misalignment, compliance barriers, or unintended socioeconomic consequences that go beyond environmental considerations. This includes considerations for both the regulated community and key industry stakeholders such as certified installers, professional engineers, project managers, consultants, and manufacturers. The Contractor must assess the most common and practical procedures currently used in the industry for the installation, maintenance, including leak detection options, and decommissioning of various types of storage tank systems located in Canada. The Contractor must review applicable requirements under the National Fire Code of Canada (NFCC), CSA B139 Installation Code for Oil-Burning Equipment, the CCME Code of Practice, and any other authority having jurisdiction (AHJ) with best requirements for protecting against fuel contamination. Term. The period of the Contract is from date of Contract (est. October 1, 2026) to December 31, 2027, inclusive. Resource Categories The resource categories (roles)* required are as follows: 1. Licensed Professional Engineer 2. Petroleum Storage Tank System Technician 3. Petroleum Storage Tank Systems Compliance Specialist 4. Project Manager *As part of its proposed Project Team, the Offeror can propose the same resource for any of the resource categories required, with the exception that the Licensed Professional Engineer cannot be the same proposed resource as the Petroleum Storage Tank System Technician. Note to Offerors: The proposed resource title (resource categories) in Annex Technical Criteria are descriptive labels intended solely to indicate the nature of the expertise required. They do not represent formal occupational classifications or restrict the number of resources proposed, the allocation of responsibilities, or the manner in which an Offeror structures its Project Team.

title: RFP National Combat Rations Program Long Term Solutions
description: CanadaBuys Notice of Proposed Procurement (NPP) / Avis de projet de marché (APM) AchatsCanada Please note that late submissions will not be considered or accepted. Public Works and Government Services Canada (PWGSC), on behalf of its client, the Department of National Defence (DND), has a requirement under the National Combat Ration Program (NCRP) to procure shelf stable combat rations in accordance with the Statement of Requirement. This requirement is to support Canadian Armed Forces (CAF) training, domestic operations, deployed operations, and emergency situations where the provision of fresh rations is not feasible. Combat rations are consumable, shelf stable products consisting of various food and non food items packaged in an overwrap bag. To fulfil this requirement, Canada has issued one Requests for Proposal (RFP) representing two procurement approaches: •a Prime Vendor approach, under which a single contractor would be responsible for managing all components of the requirement; OR •a Category by Category approach, under which multiple contracts would be awarded by component category, including the designation of a contractor responsible for ration assembly. title: France – Engineering studies – PRESTATIONS D'ASSISTANCE TECHNIQUE GENERALE POUR LES BESOINS DE LA RTM (2 LOTS)
description: La présente consultation vise la passation d'une procédure ayant pour objet les prestations suivantes : réalisation de diverses missions d'assistance technique dans le cadre de divers projets de travaux portés par la Régie des Transports métropolitains, RTM (2 lots). La consultation est décomposée en 2 lots ci-après énoncés : - Lot n°1 - Assistance technique relative à des bâtiments, ouvrages divers et installations techniques propres aux sites d'exploitation de transport ferroviaire, de métro et de tramway ; - Lot n°2 - Assistance technique relative à des infrastructures, ouvrages divers et installations techniques propres aux sites d'exploitation de transport routier de voyageurs. Les prestations à réaliser sont décrites et s'exécutent conformément aux dispositions du CCAP ainsi que du CCTP communs à tous les lots. Les présents marchés publics sont passés selon une procédure avec négociation, en application des articles L2124-3, R2124-4 et R2161-21 à R2161-23 du Code. Il s’agit d’accords-cadres au sens des articles L2125-1.1° et R2162-2 et suivants du Code. Chaque accord-cadre est conclu avec un seul opérateur économique et s’exécute par la conclusion de marchés subséquents pour les besoins dont toutes les stipulations contractuelles ne sont pas fixées dans les documents de l’accord-cadre (conformément aux articles R2162-7, R2162-11 et R2162-12 du Code). Les prestations d’assistance à maîtrise d’ouvrage donnant lieu à la conclusion de marchés subséquents sont rémunérées à prix unitaires, sur la base du bordereau des prix unitaires (BPU) de chacun des lots. Les prix indiqués au BPU constituent des prix plafonds pour la conclusion des marchés subséquents. En application de l’article R2162-4 du Code, les prestations d’assistance à maîtrise d’ouvrage faisant l’objet de marchés subséquents sont conclus sans montant minimum d’engagement et avec un montant maximum d’engagement sur sa durée initiale (1 an), à savoir : - Lot 1 : 2 000 000 € HT ; - Lot 2 : 2 000 000 € HT. Pour chaque période de reconduction, le montant maximum d’engagement est de : - Lot 1 : 2 000 000 € HT ; - Lot 2 : 2 000 000 € HT. Ce montant maximum d’engagement s’applique exclusivement aux prestations exécutées au moyen de marchés subséquents et n’inclut pas les prestations de pilotage rémunérées à prix forfaitaire. Les prestations de pilotage de l’accord-cadre, telles que décrites au CCTP, sont rémunérées sous la forme d’un prix global et forfaitaire, dans les conditions définies par la décomposition du prix global et forfaitaire (DPGF) de chacun des lots. Ces prestations sont exécutées directement dans le cadre de l’accord-cadre et ne donnent pas lieu à la conclusion de marchés subséquents. Il s’agit de marchés publics de prestations intellectuelles qui se réfèrent au Cahier des Clauses Administratives Générales applicable aux marchés publics de prestations intellectuelles (CCAG/PI), approuvé par l’arrêté du 30 mars 2021. Cette pièce générale réputée connue par les entreprises est non fournie dans le présent dossier.

title: R499--RFI School Enrollment Reporting
description: RFI Digital GI Bill and Education Service Automation & Modernization 2 EDUCATION SERVICE DEPARTMENT OF VETERANS AFFAIRS (VA) Veterans Benefits Administration (VBA) Digital GI Bill (DGIB) and Education Service School Reporting to VBA Date: August 11, 2026 Request for Information Request for Information GI Bill and Education Service School Data Exchange with VBA Introduction: The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is seeking industry input on solutions to enable secure, standardized data exchange with educational institutions in order to (1) measure the full range of outcomes GI Bill beneficiaries achieve including graduation, persistence, and post-completion employment and earnings and (2) strengthen VBA's ability to proactively identify compliance risks, including violations such as the 85/15 Rule and other indicators of fraud, waste, and abuse. Any proposed solution must minimize reporting burden on schools and training providers and be capable of scaling to accommodate new data requirements as legislative and program needs evolve. This is a Request for Information (RFI) issued for conducting market research and for eliciting industry input as to the Government s requirement to gather/obtain and communicate with educational institutions about students enrolled in the VBA s educational programs. Accordingly, this RFI constitutes neither a Request for Proposal/Quote (RFP/RFQ) nor a guarantee that one will ever be issued by the Government; furthermore, it does not commit the Government to contract for any services described herein. Do not submit a Quote/Proposal. The VA is not, at this time, seeking proposals or quotes, and therefore will not accept, review, or evaluate unsolicited proposals or quotes received in response hereto. This notice is not to be construed as a commitment on the part of the Government to award a contract/order, nor does the Government intend to pay for any information submitted because of this request. The Government does not reimburse respondents for any costs associated with the submission of the information being requested, or reimburse expenses incurred for responses to this RFI. Please do not include a price or proposal in your response. The information provided may be used by VA in developing its acquisition strategy and Performance Work Statement (PWS). Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future RFP/RFQ, if issued. Any information submitted by respondents to this RFI is strictly voluntary; however, any information received shall become the property of the Government and will not be returned to the respondent. Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary, restricted, or competition sensitive information contained in their response. This is a request for information and does not obligate the Government in any way, nor does it commit the Government to any specific course of action. Background: The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Benefits Administration (VBA), administers education benefits under the GI Bill® program, serving Veterans, servicemembers, and their dependents annually across thousands of educational institutions nationwide. These benefits spanning Chapters 30, 33, 35, and 1606 of Title 38, U.S. Code represent a significant investment in the academic and professional futures of those who have served our country. The current Digital GI Bill (DGIB) ecosystem houses VBA's claims processing systems and supporting data infrastructure. This includes the Data Mart, which houses all education (EDU) benefits data, and CorpDB, which houses all VBA data and enables VBA to produce additional on-demand reports as needed. Despite the scale and importance of these benefits, VBA currently has limited visibility into student outcomes beyond the point of enrollment certification. The data VBA receives from educational institutions today is largely transactional in nature focused on enrollment status, credit hours, and tuition costs and does not provide the longitudinal outcome data necessary to assess whether GI Bill beneficiaries are successfully completing their programs of study, persisting term over term, or achieving the academic and professional outcomes the program is intended to support. Public Law 114-315, Section 404, requires educational institutions that receive payments under the Post-9/11 GI Bill® to report academic progress to VA. Additionally, Executive Order 13607 (2012) requires VA to develop a comprehensive strategy for Servicemember and Veteran student outcome measures that are comparable, to the maximum extent practicable, across federal military and Veterans educational benefit programs. VA has previously explored outcome measure types such as retention rate, persistence rate, transfer-out rate, graduation rate, and certificate of completion, and welcomes industry input on additional or alternative approaches to satisfying these requirements. This data gap has meaningful consequences across two critical areas: Outcome Measurement VBA is committed to understanding whether GI Bill education benefits are producing positive, measurable outcomes for Veterans and their dependents not only during enrollment, but beyond it. Without reliable, standardized data from educational institutions and other authoritative sources on indicators such as graduation rates, academic persistence, program completion, and post-completion outcomes including employment and earnings, VBA cannot fully assess program effectiveness, identify areas for improvement, or demonstrate the full impact of GI Bill investments on Veterans' academic and professional success. Compliance Oversight VBA has a statutory responsibility to ensure that GI Bill benefits are administered in accordance with applicable laws and regulations, and that educational institutions participating in the program meet required standards including compliance with the 85/15 Rule and other statutory and regulatory requirements. Enhanced data exchange with educational institutions would allow VBA to proactively identify discrepancies between school-reported data and VA records, detect potential fraud, waste, and abuse earlier, and support audit and oversight functions. Beyond protecting Veterans and their dependents from bad actors within the program, this enhanced visibility would also allow VBA to recognize and champion educational institutions that consistently demonstrate strong outcomes and program compliance. To address these gaps, VBA is exploring industry recommendations and guidance on solutions that would enable secure, standardized, and scalable data exchange between educational institutions, other public and private entities and VBA. The envisioned solution would allow schools to provide VBA with structured outcome and enrollment data on GI Bill beneficiaries on a regular basis, reducing manual reporting burden on School Certifying Officials (SCOs) while significantly enhancing VBA's ability to measure program outcomes and fulfill its compliance mission. title: MRTC Parking Lot Refresh
description: Marine Forces Special Operations Command, (MARSOC), Marine Raider Center (MRC), Camp Lejeune, NC has a requirement to repair/fill cracks and seal approximately 130,000 square feet of parking lot at RR450 parking lots. The general scope of work includes cleaning, filling, smoothing, and sealing both parking lots around RR450. The following Objectives are provided: 1. Mandatory Site Visit and Base Access Requirements A mandatory site visit will be conducted on 27 August at 0900 EST at the Building RR450 parking lot, Stone Bay, MCB Camp Lejeune, NC. Mandatory Attendance: Attendance at this site visit is mandatory. Only those vendors who attend the site visit in its entirety will be eligible to submit quotes in response to this solicitation. Quotes received from vendors who did not attend the site visit will be rejected without evaluation. Base Access Request Deadline: To gain access to the MARFORSOC compound at Stone Bay, contractor personnel must be vetted. Vendors must submit their base access request documentation to the Contracting Officer (Samuel Williams) and the Contract Specialist via email no later than 24 August. Access Request Content: The access request must be submitted on the visiting company's official stationery, signed by a company authority, and contain the following information for each attendee (limit of 2 attendees per company): Full Legal Name (Last, First, Middle) Date of Birth Place of Birth Citizenship Driver's License Number and State of Issuance 2. Proposal Submission Instructions Eligible offerors (who attended the mandatory site visit) shall submit their proposals via email to the Contracting Office. Proposals must be submitted in three (3) separate and distinct volumes as outlined below. Page limits must be strictly adhered to; any pages exceeding the limit will not be evaluated. Volume Title Page Limit Submission Requirements Volume I Technical Capability 6 Pages Max Technical Approach, Equipment List, Personnel Overview, and Draft Construction Phasing Plan. Volume II Past Performance 2 Pages Max Up to three (3) Past Performance References of similar scope and complexity. Volume III Price No Limit Completed SF 1449 Schedule of Supplies/Services, Price Breakdown, and Representations & Certifications. 3. Volume Content Requirements A. Volume I: Technical Capability The Technical Volume must clearly demonstrate the offeror's capability to perform the requirements set forth in the Statement of Work (SOW). Boilerplate or repeating the SOW language without detail is unacceptable. The volume must include: Technical Approach: A detailed narrative describing how the offeror will execute SOW Objectives #1 through #6, specifically outlining the crack cleaning process, crack-filling application (Objective #2), seal coat application and mixing ratio (Objective #3), restriping and stenciling (Objective #4), parking block replacement and installation (Objective #5), and the handicap sign post installations (Objective #6). Draft Construction Phasing Plan: A draft plan showing how the offeror will execute the work while maintaining at least fifty percent (50%) parking capacity operational continuity at Building RR450 at all times. The plan must include a tentative Gantt chart schedule within the 120-day Period of Performance and explain how emergency vehicle access will be guaranteed. Security and Base Access Compliance: A brief statement acknowledging and demonstrating a plan to comply with Camp Lejeune base access regulations (NCIC checks) and coordinating with MARSOC-provided escorts. B. Volume II: Past Performance Offerors shall submit up to three (3) past performance references for federal, state, local, or commercial contracts executed within the past three (3) years that are similar in scope and complexity to the RR450 requirement (e.g., parking lot sealing, crack filling, and striping requirements exceeding 50,000 sq ft). Each reference must include: Contract Number, Customer Name, and Point of Contact (Email and Phone). Period of Performance and Total Contract Dollar Value. A brief description of the work performed, highlighting similarities to the RR450 scope of work, specifically mentioning the total square footage treated and whether phasing or escort requirements were managed. Note: Offerors may submit standard reference letters in lieu of, or in addition to, the contact list. C. Volume III: Price The offeror shall submit a fully completed SF 1449 schedule with firm-fixed-prices (FFP) for the single, lump-sum CLIN (0001). The offeror must also submit a supporting price breakdown detailing direct material costs, direct labor costs (complying with Davis-Bacon Wage Determination No. NC20260090), mobilization, project management/overhead, and bond costs.

title: FY26 Medical University of South Carolina (MUSC) Pump Upfit
description: FY26 Medical University of South Carolina (MUSC) Stormwater Pump Station - DESCRIPTION OF WORK: The Medical University of South Carolina (MUSC) stormwater pump station (PS), located in the Medical District on the Charleston Peninsula, is critical infrastructure for the City of Charleston (City). The MUSC drainage basin forms a topographic low point without a natural outlet, and the PS is required to facilitate drainage. Proposed improvements include: increased pumping capacity including both pump and discharge piping capacity; improved hydraulic configuration in the wet well and inflow chamber; enclosure and conditioning of the control room; elevating all critical electrical and HVAC equipment above the design flood elevation; replacement and upgrade of electrical, instrumentation and controls, security, and lighting; construction of a new transformer pad and installation of increased capacity transformer; replacement of both wet well inflow pipes to correct pipe slope; structural supports of pipes and transformer pad; construction of a permanent bypass connection; replacement of the chain link gate; and minor grading and landscaping around the perimeter slab. The project also includes temporary pumps and piping to maintain station operations during construction. MAGNITUDE OF WORK is estimated at: $5,000,000 TO $10,000,000 North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code: 237110, Water and Sewer Line Related THIS ACQUISITION IS UNRESTRICTED. description: Bei dem Brückenbauwerk aus dem Jahre 1918 handelt es sich um eine Fachwerkbrücke mit 18 Überbauten in Trog- und Deckkonstruktion mit Tonnenblechen. The purpose of this acquisition is to secure permanent housing of approximately 130 NHPs and the responsibility for providing them with a safe, compliant, and humane long-term sanctuary with a limited lead time. The contractor shall implement structured social group formation, behavioral rehabilitation, provide comprehensive lifetime care, and have sole custody and ownership for each animal. The overall objective is to ensure the seamless and humane transfer of all CDC animals into naturalistic and enriched environments that support their physical and behavioral health, within facilities that are compliant with standards set by the GFAS and that maintain these animals as set by applicable animal welfare regulations and standards. The facility must be GFAS-accredited and a sanctuary at which no research or breeding will take place. The facility must not buy, sell, or trade animals or sell animal byproducts. Direct public contact should be prohibited. The facility shall also provide species-appropriate habitat and enclosure design that supports the expression of natural behaviors.

title: Perforated Window Film
description: This contract is in support of the United States Marine Corps Recruiting Command (MCRC) Branding Program for each of the six (6) Marine Corps Districts (MCD), which are located throughout the United States, overseas and its territories. The use of branded locations, emphasizing the approved Marine Corps colors, symbols, themes, furnishings, and lighting effects will help distinguish Marine Corps recruiting offices from recruiting offices of other Armed Services, providing a distinct recruiting advantage vis-a-vis other Services. The appearance of the branded offices leaves a positive impression not just with prospects, but their parents and other influencers as well. MCRC is taking steps to improve physical security of recruiting facilities. MCRC intends to utilize perforated window film on the glass surfaces of storefront recruiting facilities in order to provide concealment, more specifically, protection from observation. It is necessary to have a means of obscuring the view of Marine recruiting station from the outside as a force protection measure. It is also necessary that, where practical, the Marines maintain visibility of the area outside of their office in order to maintain their situational awareness. This will provide them with the possibility of early warning, if a potential aggressor is approaching the office or preparing to commit some type of hostile or unlawful act, outside the office. Perforated window film will allow for MCRC Branding Program success, while providing increased security for recruiting personnel and individuals visiting recruiting offices. As a part of this requirement, the current storefront glass graphics will be removed, and new perforated window film will be installed to span the entire glass window/door surface. Perforated window film will be installed on existing facilities that have no storefront graphics. Additionally, perforated film will be replaced on existing facilities as required.

title: Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health (ARPA-H) Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR)/Small Business Technology Transfer (STTR) Program
description: The Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health (ARPA-H) is soliciting proposals from small business concerns (SBCs) that possess the research and development (R&D) expertise to conduct innovative research that will contribute toward ARPA-H mission needs, Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR), and Small Business Technology Transfer (STTR) program objectives. Please see the cover page of the attachment "SBIR_STTR_BAA_FY26" for applicable Stage 1 and Stage 2 deadlines for each open topic. Please see the Attachment H "ARPA-H_SBP_Government_Answered_Questions" for responses to the Q&A period. The purposes of the SBIR and STTR programs are to: (a) stimulate technological innovation; (b) strengthen the role of small business in meeting Federal research/research & development (R/R&D) needs; (c) foster and encourage participation by socially and economically disadvantaged small business concerns and women-owned business concerns; and (d) increase private sector commercialization of innovations derived from Federal R/R&D, thereby increasing competition, productivity and economic growth. For purposes of the SBIR and STTR programs, a small business concern is any business concern that, on the date of award, (1) is organized for profit, with a place of business located in the United States, which operates primarily within the United States or which makes a significant contribution to the United States economy through payment of taxes or use of American products, materials or labor; (2) is in the legal form of an individual proprietorship, partnership, limited liability company, corporation, joint venture, association, trust or cooperative, except that where the form is a joint venture, there must be less than 50 percent participation by foreign business entities in the joint venture; (3) more than 50% directly owned and controlled by one or more individuals (who are citizens or permanent resident aliens of the United States), other business concerns (each of which is more than 50% directly owned and controlled by individuals who are citizens or permanent resident aliens of the United States), or any combination of these; OR more than 50% owned by multiple venture capital operating companies, hedge funds, private equity firms, or any combination of these. No single venture capital operating company, hedge fund, or private equity firm may own more than 50% of the concern; AND, (4) has, including its affiliates, no more than 500 employees. Note: This size standard is established by law for the SBIR program, regardless of the NAICS Code assigned. See 13 C.F.R. � 121.702. THE FOLLOWING ARE THE CURRENTLY OPEN RESEARCH TOPICS. PLEASE SEE SECTION 8 OF THE BAA FOR FURTHER INFORMATION ARPA-H 01 -?Development of an annual test to inform women about their future fertility?-?The purpose of this topic is to discover new biomarkers that provide women with actionable data for fertility planning.? Results from this work will help inform the program manager regarding the feasibility of future programs focused on enhancing natural fertility before the need of IVF and guiding the development of women�s health monitoring and improvement tools. This work will develop a diagnostic test that can assess fertility status and generate an estimated timeline for the onset of infertility. This topic seeks to develop a test that is affordable, suitable for at least annual use, and provides user-friendly results for patients and care teams to support childbearing decisions.??? ARPA-H 02 -?Versatile Bioadhesives?- The purpose of this topic is to develop next-generation bioadhesive platforms that can safely and reliably seal, bond, and repair a wide range of tissues in challenging clinical conditions, including wet, bloody, and mechanically dynamic environments. These platforms may also be designed to deliver biologics or small molecules as part of treatment. title: France – Construction work for buildings relating to health – Marché global sectoriel relatif au projet de construction neuve du centre hospitalier SMR (soins médicaux de réadaptation) de Maubreuil à Saint Herblain
description: Le Centre Hospitalier de Maubreuil offre une prise en charge en soins médicaux de réadaptation (SMR). Il dispose pour cela d’un plateau technique spécialisé de rééducation. Ce dernier prévoit d’augmenter sa capacité d’accueil, tant pour l’hospitalisation conventionnelle que pour l’hôpital de jour, tout en intégrant des spécialités en oncologie. Ce projet se matérialise par la construction d’un nouveau centre hospitalier sur un terrain nu, situé à proximité de l’Hôpital G&R Laennec à Saint-Herblain. Cette construction neuve devra accueillir 96 lits et 53 places, sur une surface utile programmée de 6 913 m². La présente consultation a pour objet la contractualisation d’un marché global sectoriel au sens de l’article L.2171-5 du Code de la Commande publique. Le marché regroupe d’une part l’ensemble des études de conception nécessaires à la réalisation des ouvrages, d’autre part, l’exécution de l’ensemble des travaux nécessaires à la réalisation de ces ouvrages, et enfin la maintenance et le gros entretien et renouvellement des ouvrages sur une période de 2 années, intégrant la durée de la garantie.

title: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI)/ SOURCES SOUGHT Space Force Mission Delta 9 (MD9) � SL-5 EC2-S Ground System Sustainment
description: DESCRIPTION: The United States Space Force (USSF), Space Acquisition & Integration Office (SAIO), on behalf of Space Force Mission Delta 9 (MD9) at Schriever Space Force Base, CO and Kirkland Air Force Base, NM, is issuing this Request for Information (RFI)/ Sources Sought notice as an ongoing market research. The purpose of this notice is to identify capable industry partners, gauge market interest, and obtain direct industry feedback on our upcoming sustainment strategy. Due to the critical security requirements of the EC2-S Ground System Enclave, the draft acquisition documents are restricted and will not be posted publicly. Current contract efforts are being performed under contract number FA8818-20-D-0009. To maintain security and operational integrity, the Government will release these draft materials exclusively to qualified industry partners. To receive the draft documents, interested contractors must first submit an unclassified Capability Statement and complete the online RFI questionnaire. Once both prerequisites are met and security credentials are successfully verified, the Government will transmit the draft documents over secure channels. SCOPE OF THE MD9 EFFORT: MD9 is operationally responsible for guaranteeing mission readiness, ensuring continuous operational availability, and securing ground architecture for critical space assets. The EC2-S Ground System Enclave supports critical missions, including Surveillance LEO-5 (SL-5) and the Quasi-Zenith Satellite System-Hosted Payloads (QZSS-HP). SL-5 is a predominantly unclassified system, allowing for flexible coordination outside of SAPF spaces. However, the lack of an integrated sustainment partner encompassing systems engineering, proactive cybersecurity monitoring, and responsive technical support has led to increased systemic risks: Unintegrated Sustainment Execution across Program Management and Systems Engineering disciplines. Configuration Management & Cybersecurity Drift under high-tempo mission windows. Inconsistent Tier II/III Engineering Support challenging the operational availability threshold. Training and Documentation Lags when ground baselines evolve. The Government seeks a prime contractor capable of delivering cohesive, full-lifecycle sustainment to mitigate these risks and stabilize the EC2-S baseline. 13 Aug 2026_Updated: Key Information was updated as follows: Corrected the interactive survey link Added Kirkland AFB, NM as the addtional location Updated the closeout time from 12 PM MST to 11AM MST Added JWICS account as an alternative access channel Provided the current contract number: FA8818-20-D-0009 GATED ACCESS TO DRAFT DOCUMENTS: The draft acquisition documents are controlled and will only be released to organizations that successfully complete the unclassified submission and security vetting process outlined in this post. Because these draft documents contain sensitive acquisition and operational parameters, they will be transmitted exclusively via secure channels (SIPRNET and/or JWICS). Therefore, requesting organizations must provide a valid SIPR and/or JWICS email address with the initial submission capability. The following draft documents will be released successful vetting: Draft Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) Framework: Outlines the planned multi-phase, innovative acquisition approach for Mission Delta 9. Draft Area of Interest (AOI) - EC2-S Ground System Sustainment: Details the operational scenario, Technical Focus Areas, and contractor instructions. Draft Work Breakdown Structure (WBS): Provides the hierarchical framework for tracking program execution, deliverables, and cost elements. Draft Update to Legacy Performance Work Statement (PWS): Captures the updated baseline requirements, transitioning legacy ground system tasks into the modernized EC2-S sustainment structure. SECURITY THRESHOLD: Personnel requesting, receiving and reviewing these draft documents must possess an active Top Secret/ Sensitive Compartmented Information (TS/SCI) clearance with Special Access Program (SAP) eligibility. QUESTIONS TO INDUSTRY (FEEDBACK QUESTIONNAIRE): To streamline the collection and analysis of industry feedback, the Government is using a two-phased questionnaire process: Initial Intake Questionnaire (Open Channels): Completion of this questionnaire is a mandatory prerequisite receiving the secure draft acquisition documents. Interested parties must submit their organizational profiles, security credentials, and initial capability responses using the secure portal linked below: SAIO MD9 EC2-S_ Ground System Sustainment _ Initial Intake RFI Questionnaire � Prefilled form (Highlight, Copy, & Paste Link in browser for access) https://forms.osi.apps.mil/r/c27QFA6tdu This initial form is structured to gather corporate capabilities, clearance levels, facility security parameters, and confirmation of active SIPRNET and/or JWICS access. Follow-up Technical Feedback Questionnaire (Secure Channels): Once cleared vendors receive and review the restricted draft documents (CSO, AOI, WBS, and PWS), a detailed follow-up questionnaire will be provided via secure channels (SIPRNET and/or JWICS) for industry to submit their formal feedback, recommendations, and pricing strategy inputs on the draft package directly to the established point of contact. SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS: Interested parties must execute a phased process to complete security vetting, request the draft documents, and submit final feedback. Please complete the initial intake online questionnaire and submit an Unclassified Capability Statement to the following address: rosalind.davis.3@spaceforce.mil. CRITICAL NOTICE: Detailed, multi-page narrative technical white papers are not being requested and will not be accepted at this time. To participate in this RFI and receive the draft materials, respondents must complete the following steps: Step 1: Submit Entry Requirements (Unclassified Capability Statement & Initial Questionnaire) To initiate the request for the draft documents (CSO, AOI, WBS, PWS), organizations must complete and submit both of the following unclassified items: Submit the Initial Intake Questionnaire: Access and submit the initial intake form at the SAIO MD9 EC2-S Ground System Sustainment Inital Intake RFI Questionnaire link: https://forms.osi.apps.mil/r/c27QFA6tdu Email your Unclassified Capability Statement: Email your statement to the Point of Contact listed below. Page Limit: Maximum of eight (8) pages (including the cover page). Content Focus: Outline your firm's core capabilities, relevant past performance, and corporate credentials relating to the MD9 scope. Security & SIPRNET and/or JWICS Verification: You must explicitly include your CAGE Code, Facility Clearance level, and confirm that the personnel designated to receive and review the draft files possess active TS/SCI clearances with SAP eligibility. SIPR and/or JWICS Email Requirement: You must provide a valid, active SIPR and/or JWICS email address within the Capability Statement to facilitate secure document transfer. File Format: Adobe PDF (preferred) or Microsoft Word format. Step 2: Security Verification, Document Release, & Follow-Up Feedback Upon receipt and successful verification of both the unclassified Capability Statement and the initial questionnaire, SAIO will verify the security credentials of the designated personnel. Once cleared, the Government will transmit the draft acquisition package (CSO, AOI, WBS, and PWS) directly to your organization's designated secure email over SIPRNET and/or JWCIS. Code 2: Assembly (or set or kit) not furnished - Used following detail parts. Code 3: Part not furnished separately - Use assembly. Code 4: Part redesigned - Old and new parts are completely interchangeable. Code 5: Part redesigned - New part replaces old. Old part cannot replace new. Code 6: Part redesigned - Parts not interchangeable. 3.4 Mercury Free - The material supplied under this contract/purchase order is intended for use on submarines/surface ships and therefore shall contain no metallic mercury and shall be free from mercury contamination. Mercury contamination of the material will be cause for rejection. If the inclusion of metallic mercury is required as a functional part of the material furnished under this contract, the Contractor shall obtain written approval from the Procurement Contracting Officer before proceeding with manufacture. The contractor's request shall explain in detail the requirements for mercury, identify specifically the parts to contain mercury, and explain the method of protection against mercury escape. Such a request will be forwarded directly to the Procurement Contracting Officer with a copy to the applicable Government Inspector. Upon approval by the Contracting Officer, the vendor will provide a "Warning Plate" stating that metallic mercury is a functional part of the item and will include name and location of that part. The use of mercury, mercury compounds, or mercury-bearing instruments and/or equipment in a manner which might cause contamination in the manufacture, assembly, or test of material on this contract is prohibited. The most probable causes of contamination are direct-connected manometers, mercury vacuum pumps, mercury seals, or the handling of mercury in the immediate vicinity. Mercury switches, mercury in glass thermometers, standard cells and other items containing mercury may be used if they are located so as not to constitute a contamination hazard. If external contamination by metallic mercury occurs or is suspected, the following test may be used to determine whether contamination by metallic mercury exists or whether corrective cleaning measures have been effective. Enclose the equipment in a polyethylene bag or close-fitting airtight container for eight hours at room temperature (70 degrees F minimum).Sample the trapped air and if mercury vapor concentration is 0.01 mg/cu meter or more, the material is mercury contaminated insofar as the requirements of this contract are concerned. These requirements shall be included in any subcontract or purchase order hereunder and the Contractor shall insure SubContractor compliance with these requirements. Technical questions pertaining to these requirements shall be referred to the Procurement Contracting Officer via the cognizant Administrative Contracting Officer. For background, the following information is provided: Mercury is corrosive to gold, silver, nickel, stainless steels, aluminum and copper alloys. Stainless steels, nickel, and copper alloys are widely used in reactor plants and other submarine/surface ship systems. Accidental trapping of mercury in a component could cause serious damage to vital parts. Mercury is also toxic if inhaled, ingested, or absorbed through the skin. It is evident that grave consequences could result from small amounts of mercury vapor present in an unreplenished submarine/surface ship atmosphere. 4. title: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI)/ SOURCES SOUGHT Space Force Mission Delta 9 (MD9) � SL-5 EC2-S Ground System Sustainment
description: DESCRIPTION: The United States Space Force (USSF), Space Acquisition & Integration Office (SAIO), on behalf of Space Force Mission Delta 9 (MD9) at Schriever Space Force Base, CO, is issuing this Request for Information (RFI)/ Sources Sought notice as part of an ongoing market research. The purpose of this notice is to identify capable industry partners, gauge market interest, and obtain direct industry feedback on our upcoming sustainment strategy. Due to the critical security requirements of the EC2-S Ground System Enclave, the draft acquisition documents are restricted and will not be posted publicly. To maintain security and operational integrity, the Government will release these draft materials exclusively to qualified industry partners. To receive the draft documents, interested contractors must first submit an unclassified Capability Statement and complete the online RFI questionnaire. Once both prerequisites are met and security credentials are successfully verified, the Government will transmit the draft documents over secure channels. SCOPE OF THE MD9 EFFORT: MD9 is operationally responsible for guaranteeing mission readiness, ensuring continuous operational availability, and securing ground architecture for critical space assets. The EC2-S Ground System Enclave supports critical missions, including Surveillance LEO-5 (SL-5) and the Quasi-Zenith Satellite System-Hosted Payloads (QZSS-HP). SL-5 is a predominantly unclassified system, allowing for flexible coordination outside of SAPF spaces. However, the lack of an integrated sustainment partner encompassing systems engineering, proactive cybersecurity monitoring, and responsive technical support has led to increased systemic risks: Unintegrated Sustainment Execution across Program Management and Systems Engineering disciplines. Configuration Management & Cybersecurity Drift under high-tempo mission windows. Inconsistent Tier II/III Engineering Support challenging the operational availability threshold. Training and Documentation Lags when ground baselines evolve. The Government seeks a prime contractor capable of delivering cohesive, full-lifecycle sustainment to mitigate these risks and stabilize the EC2-S baseline. GATED ACCESS TO DRAFT DOCUMENTS: The draft acquisition documents are controlled and will only be released to organizations that successfully complete the unclassified submission and security vetting process outlined in this post. Because these draft documents contain sensitive acquisition and operational parameters, they will be transmitted exclusively via secure channels (SIPRNET). Therefore, requesting organizations must provide a valid SIPR email address with the initial submission capability. The following draft documents will be released successful vetting: Draft Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) Framework: Outlines the planned multi-phase, innovative acquisition approach for Mission Delta 9. Draft Area of Interest (AOI) - EC2-S Ground System Sustainment: Details the operational scenario, Technical Focus Areas, and contractor instructions. Draft Work Breakdown Structure (WBS): Provides the hierarchical framework for tracking program execution, deliverables, and cost elements. Draft Update to Legacy Performance Work Statement (PWS): Captures the updated baseline requirements, transitioning legacy ground system tasks into the modernized EC2-S sustainment structure. SECURITY THRESHOLD: Personnel requesting, receiving and reviewing these draft documents must possess an active Top Secret/ Sensitive Compartmented Information (TS/SCI) clearance with Special Access Program (SAP) eligibility. QUESTIONS TO INDUSTRY (FEEDBACK QUESTIONNAIRE): To streamline the collection and analysis of industry feedback, the Government is using a two-phased questionnaire process: Initial Intake Questionnaire (Open Channels): Completion of this questionnaire is a mandatory prerequisite receiving the secure draft acquisition documents. Interested parties must submit their organizational profiles, security credentials, and initial capability responses using the secure portal linked below: SAIO MD9 EC2-S_ Ground System Sustainment _ Initial Intake RFI Questionnaire � Prefilled form This initial form is structured to gather corporate capabilities, clearance levels, facility security parameters, and confirmation of active SIPRNET access. Follow-up Technical Feedback Questionnaire (Secure Channels): Once cleared vendors receive and review the restricted draft documents (CSO, AOI, WBS, and PWS), a detailed follow-up questionnaire will be provided via secure channels (SIPRNET) for industry to submit their formal feedback, recommendations, and pricing strategy inputs on the draft package directly to the established point of contact. SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS: Interested parties must execute a phased process to complete security vetting, request the draft documents, and submit final feedback. Please complete the initial intake online questionnaire and submit an Unclassified Capability Statement to the following address: rosalind.davis.3@spaceforce.mil. CRITICAL NOTICE: Detailed, multi-page narrative technical white papers are not being requested and will not be accepted at this time. To participate in this RFI and receive the draft materials, respondents must complete the following steps: Step 1: Submit Entry Requirements (Unclassified Capability Statement & Initial Questionnaire) To initiate the request for the draft documents (CSO, AOI, WBS, PWS), organizations must complete and submit both of the following unclassified items: Submit the Initial Intake Questionnaire: Access and submit the initial intake form at the SAIO MD9 EC2-S Ground System Sustainment Inital Intake RFI Questionnaire link. Email your Unclassified Capability Statement: Email your statement to the Point of Contact listed below. Page Limit: Maximum of eight (8) pages (including the cover page). Content Focus: Outline your firm's core capabilities, relevant past performance, and corporate credentials relating to the MD9 scope. Security & SIPRNET Verification: You must explicitly include your CAGE Code, Facility Clearance level, and confirm that the personnel designated to receive and review the draft files possess active TS/SCI clearances with SAP eligibility. SIPR Email Requirement: You must provide a valid, active SIPR email address within the Capability Statement to facilitate secure document transfer. File Format: Adobe PDF (preferred) or Microsoft Word format. Step 2: Security Verification, Document Release, & Follow-Up Feedback Upon receipt and successful verification of both the unclassified Capability Statement and the initial questionnaire, SAIO will verify the security credentials of the designated personnel. Once cleared, the Government will transmit the draft acquisition package (CSO, AOI, WBS, and PWS) directly to your organization's designated secure email over SIPRNET. Follow-Up Feedback: After reviewing the draft files, contractors will receive a follow-up feedback questionnaire via secure channels (SIPRNET) to submit their technical inputs, structural recommendations, and answers to specific acquisition strategy questions. Deadlines & Schedule: Prerequisite Submission Deadline (Capability Statement & Questionnaire): Submissions should be executed as early as possible to allow the Government to vet clearances and complete the secure transfer of files over SIPRNET. RFI Final Response & Closing Deadline: All entry requirements and initial requests must be completed and submitted no later than September 11, 2026, at 12:00 PM MST. DISCLAIMER & IMPORTANT NOTES: This RFI is issued solely for information and planning purposes and does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFP in the future. This RFI does not commit the US Government to contract for any supply or service whatsoever. All costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the interested party�s expense. Cage _______ ref. no. ;90099 1941E15-002; 3.2 Marking - This item shall be physically identified in accordance with ;MIL-STD-130, REV N, 16 NOV 2012; . 3.3 Changes in Design, Material Servicing, or Part Number - Except for a Code 1 change, which shall be processed as provided in the code statement shown below, no substitution of items shall be made until the NAVICP-MECH Contracting Officer has notified and approval has been given by issuance of a written change order. When any change in design, material, servicing or part number is made to replace or substitute any item to be furnished on this contract/purchase order, the Contractor shall furnish, for the substituting/replacement item, a drawing and an explanation of the reason for the change, explaining the reason therefor. If finished detail drawings are not available, shop drawings in the form used by the manufacturer will be acceptable for Government evaluation. When notifying the Procurement Contracting Officer of the reasons for making substitutions, the type of change shall be indicated by code number in accordance with one of the following statements: Code 1: PART NUMBER CHANGE ONLY - If the Manufacturer's Part Number indicated thereon has changed, but the parts are identical in all respects, supply the item and advise NAVICP-MECH immediately of the new part number. Code 2: Assembly (or set or kit) not furnished - Used following detail parts. Code 3: Part not furnished separately - Use assembly. Code 4: Part redesigned - Old and new parts are completely interchangeable. Code 5: Part redesigned - New part replaces old. Old part cannot replace new. Code 6: Part redesigned - Parts not interchangeable. 3.4 Mercury Free - The material supplied under this contract/purchase order is intended for use on submarines/surface ships and therefore shall contain no metallic mercury and shall be free from mercury contamination. Mercury contamination of the material will be cause for rejection. If the inclusion of metallic mercury is required as a functional part of the material furnished under this contract, the Contractor shall obtain written approval from the Procurement Contracting Officer before proceeding with manufacture. The contractor's request shall explain in detail the requirements for mercury, identify specifically the parts to contain mercury, and explain the method of protection against mercury escape. Such a request will be forwarded directly to the Procurement Contracting Officer with a copy to the applicable Government Inspector. Upon approval by the Contracting Officer, the vendor will provide a "Warning Plate" stating that metallic mercury is a functional part of the item and will include name and location of that part. The use of mercury, mercury compounds, or mercury-bearing instruments and/or equipment in a manner which might cause contamination in the manufacture, assembly, or test of material on this contract is prohibited. The most probable causes of contamination are direct-connected manometers, mercury vacuum pumps, mercury seals, or the handling of mercury in the immediate vicinity. Mercury switches, mercury in glass thermometers, standard cells and other items containing mercury may be used if they are located so as not to constitute a contamination hazard. If external contamination by metallic mercury occurs or is suspected, the following test may be used to determine whether contamination by metallic mercury exists or whether corrective cleaning measures have been effective. Enclose the equipment in a polyethylene bag or close-fitting airtight container for eight hours at room temperature (70 degrees F minimum).Sample the trapped air and if mercury vapor concentration is 0.01 mg/cu meter or more, the material is mercury contaminated insofar as the requirements of this contract are concerned. These requirements shall be included in any subcontract or purchase order hereunder and the Contractor shall insure SubContractor compliance with these requirements. Technical questions pertaining to these requirements shall be referred to the Procurement Contracting Officer via the cognizant Administrative Contracting Officer. For background, the following information is provided: Mercury is corrosive to gold, silver, nickel, stainless steels, aluminum and copper alloys. Louisiana Agriculture and Forestry licensed Arborist is still required by state law. It is recommended offerors visit the site to gain a thorough understanding of the requirement. Once the highest technically rated offeror is identified, their price will be evaluated to determine whether it is fair and reasonable. Past performance will also be assessed to ensure it is acceptable or neutral. Anticipated award will be a firm fixed price purchae order with a 60 day period of performance.

title: Diplomatic Courier Support Services - Women-Owned Small Business (WOSB) Set-Aside
description: DIPLOMATIC COURIER SUPPORT SERVICES - WOMEN-OWNED SMALL BUSINESS (WOSB) SET-ASIDE The Government encourages responsible WOSB concerns to review this notice and submit an offer in response to this combined synopsis/solicitation. Interested WOSB concerns should ensure that their: SAM.gov registration is active; UEI information is current; NAICS code information is current; Representations and certifications are current; Applicable facility and personnel security capabilities are established or obtainable; and Proposal response is in accordance with the soliciation and supporting documents attached herein. 1. CLASSIFICATION CODE - M1GZ 2. NAICS CODE - 492110 Small Business Size Standard: 1,500 employees 3. CONTRACTING OFFICE - U.S. Department of State, Bureau of Global Acquisitions 4. CONTRACT INFORMATION - The U.S. Department of State, Bureau of Global Acquisitions hereby issues a combined synopsis and solicitation for Diplomatic Courier Support Services (DCSS). The acquisition is a total set-aside for Woman-Owned Small Business (WOSB) concerns eligible under the Small Business Administration (SBA) WOSB Federal Contract Program. The Government anticipates awarding one contract to provide Diplomatic Courier Support Services (DCSS). 5. DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT The Department of State (DOS) requires a WOSB Contractor for comprehensive operational and logistic support in support of Diplomatic Courier Services. The Contractor shall provide qualified personnel and managment support necessary to accomplish the requirements identified in the Performance Work Statement. (PWS). The awarded Contractor shall provide personnel and equipment to effectively transport inbound and outbound courier escort services in support of the Diplomatic Courier Service and supporting Diplomatic Secuity Offices around the world. The Diplomatic Courier Service operates twenty four hours a day, seven days a week. Support personnel will be required to work overtime and overnight. 6. PLACE OF PERFORMANCE The principal places of performance for the contract is as follows: State Annex (SA) 8 7000 Loisdale RoadSpringfield, VA 22150, Miami Courier Division 2261 NW 66th Ave. BLDG. 701 Miami, FL 33122, and SRD2 20622 Sally Ride Drive Sterling VA 20164 7. CONTRACT TYPE This is a Labor Hour contract, to include ancillary Contract Line Item Numbers (CLINs): Surge Support for overtime hours worked and Other Direct Cost as cost reimbursable. 8. PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE This contract shall be effective on the date of the Contracting Officer's signature. The period of performance is a base year (12 months) and four one-year option periods. This contract shall remain in effect (if options are awarded) as follows: Base Period: November 14, 2026 through November 13, 2027 Option Period 1: November 14, 2027 through November 13, 2028 Option Period 2: November 14, 2028 through November 13, 2029 Option Period 3: November 14, 2029 through November 13, 2030 Option Period 4: November 14, 2030 through November 13, 2031 9. WOSB SET-ASIDE This acquisition is anticipated to be set aside in its entirely for WOSB concerns eligible under the SBA WOSB Federal Contract Program. Offerors must qualify as a small business concern under the applicable NAICS code and must be eligible for participation in the WOSB Federal Contract Program At the time of offer submission and award, the apparent sucessful offeror must be eligible under the WOSB Progam in accordance with applicable SBA regulations and FAR Subpart 19. The Government will verify WOSB eligibility through the System for Award Management (SAM.gov) and/or the Dynamic Small Business Search (DSBS), as applicable. A concern that is not eligible for the WOSB Program at the applicable time will not be eligible for award. 10. OFFEROR DUE DATE Offeror response due date is Friday, September 11, 2026 by 2:00 PM Eastern Standard Time. 11. QUESTIONS REGARDING SOLICITATION DUE DATE Questions are due by no later than Friday, August 28, 2026 by 11:00 Eastern Standard Time.

description: Amendment 0001 The purpose of this amendment is to post RFP Questions and Answers (see amendment attachment 1), revise provisions of the original RFP and extend the due dates by one week. ________________________________________________________________________ You are invited to submit a proposal in response to the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Langley Research Center (LaRC) for the Geostationary Littoral Imaging and Monitoring Radiometer Access to Space (GLIMR ATS) solicitation. See attached Final RFP Cover Letter and Final RFP documents for full details.

title: HEAVY MARINE EQUIPMENT LEASING AND SITE ACTIVITY SUPPORT SERVICES � STAMFORD HURRICANE BARRIER, STAMFORD, CT AND HOP BROOKE DAM, MIDDLEBURY, CT
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, New England District is issuing this Sources Sought Announcement for Services for the HEAVY MARINE EQUIPMENT LEASING AND SITE ACTIVITY SUPPORT SERVICES, STAMFORD HURRICANE BARRIER, STAMFORD, CT and HOP BROOK DAM, MIDDLEBURY[ED1] , CT. This announcement is to determine interest, availability and capability of Small and Large Business concerns for this project. The NAICS code for this procurement is 532412. *NOTE: If interested firms find a different NAICS code is more suitable for the type of work mentioned, they are urged to include suggested NAICS in the capabilities package. * The project is planned to be issued in the FALL of 2026 with work to take place in the WINTER/SPRING of 2027. The estimated project cost is between $1,000,000 - $5,000,000. PROJECT SCOPE: The Contractor shall provide ancillary support, site preparation, and heavy equipment leasing services at the Stamford Hurricane Barrier and Hop Brook Dam. Key work components of the Performance Work Statement may include: Furnishing and operating critical maritime and heavy equipment assets. The detailed list may include, but will not be limited to the following: 250-ton floating crane with an operator Material and handling work barges Note: Work barges must be capable of operating within a navigational channel width of 90 feet (bathymetry data is available) All-terrain 90-ton crane with an operator (to assist in swinging materials into the barrier house Vacuum trucks (for debris clean out of the gate�s interior) Man lifts/telehandlers Underwater lifting bags Dewatering pumps Supplementary rental generators or compressors Necessary rigging for lifting operations Providing, operating, and maintaining all necessary confined-space safety equipment, including forced-air pumps and atmospheric monitoring systems, to ensure safe working conditions during all interior barrier operations. Note: Sediment is assumed to be contaminated with specific metal concentrations that exceed Connecticut DEEP direct exposure criteria, including but not limited to Zinc (up to 35,900 mg/kg), Arsenic (up to 15.3 mg/kg), and Cadmium (up to 43.8 mg/kg), along with elevated Benzo(b)fluoranthene (PAHs). Additionally, the assumed presence of Hydrogen Sulfide (H2S) requires positive-pressure supplied air respirators for all entrants. Executing a complete debris cleanout of the hurricane barrier's interior gate (approximately 20 tons). Additional site activities include the replacement of structural anodes (approximately 225), and the installation of designated helical anchor points for the deployment of silk turbidity curtains for sediment containment in the work area. Preparing an equipment laydown and staging area at a Government-approved locations, requiring the installation of a temporary gravel pad and perimeter security fencing for the duration of the project, with minor site restoration required upon completion. Interested firms should submit a capabilities package to include the following: business classification (i.e. HUBZone, small business, etc.), as well as qualifications and experience in performing the work components stated above. The Government will be issuing a solicitation and will evaluate submissions against the following strict prequalification criteria: A minimum of five (5) years of corporate experience executing heavy marine civil construction, debris cleanouts, and marine site preparation on active navigation gates or tidal water structures. Demonstrated past performance mobilizing and operating water-based heavy lifting assets, specifically floating cranes with a minimum capacity of at least 200 tons and managing work barges in restricted navigational channels. Proven experience implementing and maintaining OSHA-compliant hazardous confined-space safety protocols, including continuous multi-gas atmospheric monitoring and forced-air ventilation systems, during interior gate chamber or barrier operations. Demonstrated experience preparing storage yards or laydown sites to safely receive, support, and secure oversized, heavy structural components. This includes staging layout design, heavy timber dunnage engineering, and site leveling. Provide at least two (2) specific project examples completed within the last seven (7) years that directly demonstrate experience in the heavy marine support elements described above. For each project, include the contract value, the client agency, and a detailed description of the marine and crane assets deployed. If subcontractors are proposed, their experience must also be documented within the same seven-year window. Proof of bonding capability is required. Responses are limited to twenty pages. Responses are due by September 11, 2026. Responses should be emailed to: Kyle.K.Hall@usace.army.mil Phone Contact: (978) 318-8479 Interested firms shall provide the above documentation in one original form and one copy. The Government will not pay for any material provided in response to this market survey nor return the data provided. This notice is for information purposes only and is not a request to be placed on a solicitation mailing list nor is it a Request for Proposal (RFP) or an announcement of a solicitation. The results of this survey will be considered to be in effect for a period of one year from the date of this notice.
